The tie at 48

Say Nothing vs. Something Rich and Strange All at 48 pts

Say Nothing and Something Rich and Strange both finished on 48 points. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head first: ignore the rest of the ballot and ask how each voter ranked these two against one another.

The head-to-head split 4–4 — dead even, no winner, nothing to separate them. That sends the tie through to the next breaker, first-place votes, where Say Nothing leads 2–1 and takes second. Both books stay on the candidate list at full strength.

Notes

The second even-split fall-through. August 2026 was the first: a pair that matched on Borda and then matched again head-to-head. A 4–4 split with eight voters is the cleanest possible way for Condorcet to say nothing at all.

Eight ballots, five different first choices. Inventing the Renaissance, Say Nothing and An Immense World took two firsts each; Something Rich and Strange and Born to Run took one apiece. Nobody ran away with the top of the ballot — the winner won on depth, not on firsts.

An Immense World is the polarizing one. It tied for the most first-place votes in the field with two, and still finished fourth on 43 points. Enough voters left it low to cost it eleven points on the leader.

Say Nothing is runner-up again — second month running, second tie running. In November it was level at the top and lost the head-to-head; this time it was level at second and won the fall-through.

No debuts. Every book on this ballot had been polled before. The field is down to nine after November's three relegations and Endurance's selection, which is why nothing was relegated this round.

The River of Doubt reaches twenty-two polls and finished last on 27 points, with no first-place votes.

Methodology

Borda count with 9 candidates: 1st place = 9 points, last place = 1 point. 8 forced-rank ballots collected via survey. Ties resolve per the club's Polling Methodology memo (formalized after the February 2026 tie): Condorcet head-to-head first, then first-place votes if pairwise cannot separate the books. This round produced a tie at 48 points, resolved by first place votes.
